title: SI units and prefixes; Electrical power and energy
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EL05-1#N.3, MS01-1#N.5, EL05-1#N.5, MS01-1#N.7, EL05-1#N.10a, MS01-1#N.9, EL05-1#N.11a, MS01-1#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Newton
items.clue: Name for kg m s⁻², from force = mass × acceleration.

items.label: Derived unit
items.clue: One obtained from a defining equation, such as m s⁻¹ for velocity.

items.label: Prefix
items.clue: Letter such as k, M or n placed before a symbol to stand for a power of ten.

items.label: Base units
items.clue: Building blocks such as kg, m, s, A, K and mol, from which all others are made.

questions.stem: The potential difference across an ohmic resistor is increased so that the current in the resistor becomes three times as large. What is the ratio of the new power dissipated in the resistor, P₂, to the original power, P₁?
questions.explanation: The resistor is ohmic, so R is unchanged. P = I²R: tripling I multiplies P by 3² = 9.

questions.stem: A spring's stiffness is its spring constant: the force needed per unit change in its length. What is the unit of the spring constant in base units?
questions.explanation: Spring constant = force ÷ change in length: kg m s⁻² ÷ m = kg s⁻². This is the same unit as N m⁻¹.

questions.stem: A steady current of 0.25 A flows in a 24 Ω resistor for 2.0 minutes. How much energy is dissipated in the resistor?
questions.explanation: Power = I²R = 0.25² × 24 = 1.5 W. Energy = power × time = 1.5 W × 120 s = 180 J.

questions.stem: The cross-sectional area of a wire is 0.50 mm². What is this area in m²?
A 3.0 kW kettle is switched on for 4.0 minutes. How much energy does it transfer, in kWh?
A kettle transfers 0.10 kW h of energy. How many joules is this?
A 60 W lamp and a 100 W lamp are both rated for a 230 V supply. They are connected in series across a 230 V supply. Assume each keeps its normal working resistance. Which lamp is brighter?

options.text: The 60 W lamp: it has the larger resistance, and in series both carry the same current.
The 100 W lamp: it has the higher power rating, so it gives more light.
The 100 W lamp: a smaller resistance gives more power, as P = V²/R.
Both are equally bright, as they carry the same current.

questions.explanation: R = V²/P: about 880 Ω for the 60 W lamp, 530 Ω for the 100 W lamp. Same current in series, so P = I²R is larger in the 60 W lamp (about 23 W against 14 W).

questions.stem: Pressure is force ÷ area, and its unit is the pascal (Pa). What is the pascal in base units?
questions.explanation: Pa = N m⁻² = kg m s⁻² × m⁻² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².
